# Strapi conventions (Strapi 5, TypeScript, SQLite)

## Content types live in code
- Every content type and component is defined as schema files under `cms/src/api/<name>/content-types/<name>/schema.json` and `cms/src/components/<category>/<name>.json`.
- Never rely on changes made only through the admin Content-Type Builder: they are not reviewable. If one is made in dev, commit the generated files.
- Use `draftAndPublish: true` for business-managed content so only published entries reach the app.
- Field names in camelCase; descriptive names (`basePrice`, not `price1`).

## Country differentiation
- The strategy is defined in the multi-country ADR in `docs/adr/`. Read it before modelling any content type and follow it exactly. Do not introduce a second mechanism.

## Querying (Strapi 5)
- Server code uses the Document Service API: `strapi.documents('api::x.x').findMany({ filters, populate, status: 'published' })`.
- REST responses in Strapi 5 are flat (no `data.attributes`); entries are identified by `documentId`.
- Populate explicitly what the frontend needs; never `populate=*` in production paths.

## Security and permissions
- The browser only reads. The Public role gets `find` / `findOne` on exactly the content types the wizard reads — nothing else, no `create/update/delete`.
- Permissions are granted in code at bootstrap (`cms/src/index.ts`), so a fresh database is configured identically. List each granted action with a comment saying why.
- No API tokens are created by code. No token of any kind reaches the frontend.
- Never read, print or commit `.env`; document new variables in `.env.example` only.

## Seed data
- Seed runs at bootstrap only when the database is empty, is idempotent, and lives in `cms/src/seed/` (one file per content type, data per country).
- Fictitious data only (no real people, documents or plates).
- Seeded entries are published so the app works right after `docker compose up`.
- An admin user for local development may be created from `.env` variables; defaults are dev-only and documented in the README.

## Contract
- The schema is the source of truth for the API contract. When a field is added/removed/renamed, report it so the Angular models in `frontend/src/app/features/*/data/` are updated in the same commit.
- Breaking changes to an existing contract require human approval (constitution §3.3).

## Verification
- `npm --prefix cms run build` must pass before reporting.

- `cms/`: Headless CMS built with Strapi 5 (TypeScript, SQLite). Content types, APIs, seed, permissions.
- `frontend/`: Angular 22 app (TypeScript, ESLint), Vitest unit tests next to the code, Playwright e2e in `frontend/e2e/`.

- `.claude/agents/`: subagent definitions. `.claude/skills/`: skills.
- `ai-logs/`: exported agent sessions. Never edit.

## Verification Commands
- **Frontend (lint + typecheck + unit tests):** `npm --prefix frontend run verify`
- **Frontend build:** `npm --prefix frontend run build`
- **Frontend e2e (Playwright):** `npm --prefix frontend run e2e`
- **CMS build / typecheck:** `npm --prefix cms run build`
- **CMS unit tests:** `npm --prefix cms test`
- **CMS dev server:** `npm --prefix cms run develop`
- **Full stack:** `docker compose up --build`

## Stack Rules (all agents)
- **Angular:** standalone components only, no NgModules; signals for state; built-in control flow (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`); typed forms; no `any`. Details: `angular-conventions` skill.
- **Strapi:** schemas defined in code; Public role gets only `find`/`findOne` on what the wizard reads. Details: `strapi-conventions` skill.
- **Security:** no Strapi token of any kind in the frontend; the browser calls only relative `/api/...` URLs (proxied by nginx / `proxy.conf.json`).
- **Layout:** Bootstrap 5.3 grid and utilities only (containers, grid, flex, spacing), never its colour, typography or component classes. Details: `ui-ux-guidelines` skill §5, ADR 0003.
- **Accessibility:** every field has a visible label; the wizard is fully keyboard-operable; works on mobile and desktop.
- **Data:** fictitious data only. No real personal data, documents, plates or credentials anywhere in the repo.

## Plan Phase Additions (Gate 2)
`plan.md` must also contain, when applicable:
- **Unit test candidates:** list the unit tests worth writing (business logic, validations, calculations, data mapping, critical interactions; never trivial rendering or getters), each with **what** it checks and **why** it matters, as a table (ID `UT-NN`, area, what, why). Table-driven tests state their example count. The human marks each one **Approved** or **Rejected** at Gate 2. Developer agents write only approved unit tests; a regression test for a bug found after Gate 2 (review finding or Gate 3 correction) is allowed and must be named in its task.
- **E2E candidates:** list only critical flows that deserve an e2e test, each with a one-line justification. The human marks each one **Approved** or **Rejected** at Gate 2. The `e2e-tester` agent runs only for approved candidates.
- **Design options:** for every client-facing view, 2–3 design options based on the `ui-ux-guidelines` skill, with a recommendation. The human picks one at Gate 2.
- **ADRs:** every architectural decision gets an ADR in `docs/adr/` (context, alternatives, consequences), linked from `plan.md`.

## Asking the Human
- Every question to the human (Gate 1 clarify questions, Gate 2 choices, stop conditions) MUST be asked with the interactive question tool (`AskUserQuestion`): one question per call, 2–4 options, the recommended one first with "(Recommended)" in its label, and a self-contained question text (the human may see only the dialog).
- Never put a question and its options only in prose: in the desktop app, text written before the end-of-turn summary can be collapsed and the human never sees it.
- After the answer, repeat the question and the chosen answer in plain text so they stay in the session log.

## Traceability
- The user story ID `US-XX` appears in: spec folder name, spec header, each task line, ADR "Related" field, test names (`describe('US-XX · FR-XXX …')`), and commit footer `Refs: US-XX`.

- Human corrections: Gate 1 in `spec.md` › Clarifications, Gate 2 in `plan.md` › Revisions, Gate 3 as new tasks in `tasks.md`.

## Security & Workflow Hygiene
- **NEVER** read, print, or commit `cms/.env` or any `.env` file (only read `.env.example` when checking required environment variables).
- The Strapi schema (`cms/src/api/`) is the source of truth for API contracts; Angular models in `frontend/src/app/features/*/data/` must match it. A schema change updates the models in the same commit.
- Never edit `.specify/templates/`, `.specify/scripts/`, `.claude/skills/speckit-*` or the constitution unless the human explicitly asks.

- [Export session logs reminder](export-session-logs-reminder.md) — remind ONCE at project end to export a single file to ai-logs/, not per story
- [Ask questions with dialog](ask-questions-with-dialog.md) — always use AskUserQuestion for decisions, never prose-only
- [Gate 3 corrections need a review round](gate3-corrections-need-review-round.md) — append a code-reviewer round to review.md per Gate 3 fix batch

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application. Finder is an application like any other: clicking the desktop, the Dock, or a Finder window (including Go to Folder) requires a Finder grant. The menu bar does not, as long as the app that is frontmost is one you have at tier "full".

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. - **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, drag-drop, and the menu bar are blocked. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, drag-drop, and the menu bar are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool. Never use it, AppleScript or other scripting to get around these limits.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

You can do much of your work through the Bash tool when it is the simpler route: read files with cat, head, or sed -n, search with grep and find, and make small, mechanical file changes with sed, heredocs, or short scripts instead of the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools. The choice is yours: prefer Edit or Write when a shell edit would be fragile, such as exact or multi-line replacements, or sed/awk flags that differ between GNU and BSD/macOS.
